content: Integrative medicine is a subset of alternative medicine that asserts its focus on methods supported by robust scientific evidence regarding their efficacy and safety. The primary advocate of integrative medicine is Dr. Andrew Weil, who established the Program in Integrative Medicine at the University of Arizona in 1994. This program was inspired by a term originally coined by Dr. Elson Haas. It is suggested that reputable providers of alternative health products, who have conducted medical studies on their products, often make these studies accessible online. Relevant publications may be found in journals such as Integrative Medicine: A Clinician's Journal and are also available through the National Library of Medicine. Functional medicine, on the other hand, was initiated by Dr. Jeffrey Bland at the Cleveland Clinic. These improvements were observed in group appointments using a shared medical appointment (SMA) format. Additionally, over a six-month period, patients at functional medicine clinics demonstrated better outcomes compared to those receiving care at the Cleveland Clinic Twinsburg Family Health Center. As of January 2022, studies registered on ClinicalTrials.gov related to functional medicine include 22 studies with functional medicine mentioned anywhere in the record, and 8 studies specifically listing functional medicine in the intervention field. However, none of these studies have posted results.
